newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: British deny contacts with Sri Lanka rebels.
newsitem.headline: British deny contacts with Sri Lanka rebels.

text.p: The British government on Saturday denied speculation that it had been involved in an peace initiative between the Sri Lankan government and separatist Tamil Tiger rebels.

"The British High Commission is concerned by the speculative nature of some of the comments in the Sri Lankan and Indian press alleging links between the British government and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE)," a statement issued by the high commission said.

It said British Under-Secretary of State Liam Fox, who last week brokered an agreement between Sri Lanka's two main political parties to work together to solve the island's ethnic war, has had no contacts with the LTTE.

"There have been allegations that Dr. Fox has spoken to the LTTE or that his visit here was in some way connected with reports of a visit by (the rebels' international spokesman) Lawrence Thilakar to the Wanni (in Sri Lanka's north)", the statement said.

It added Fox's initiative was limited to the ruling People's Alliance (PA) and main opposition United National Party (UNP), which agreed to take a "common approach" to solve Sri Lanka's protracted war with the rebels.
"At no time did Dr. Fox or the British government have any discussions about this initiative with the LTTE," the statement said.
The Sri Lankan government earlier said the agreement was not a prelude to foreign mediation in ending the war and that there were no immediate plans for talks with the LTTE.
An LTTE spokesman in London told Reuters the rebels too had no plans for peace talks with Colombo.

The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
